root_cause_summary: Investigated a sample of missed opportunities across all 7 rules present in the golden ground truth. 6 of 7 sampled misses were genuine detector coverage gaps (rule implementations hardcode narrow, same-file/same-function idioms -- specific SDK call shapes, a fixed sink taxonomy, one class-based self-judge idiom, *Action() naming conventions -- that real code routinely routes around via custom abstractions, native bridges, MCP transports, or graph-pipeline architectures); 1 of 7 was a reasonable, documented precision exclusion; 0 of 7 were ground-truth review errors. LLM-EVL-001 additionally had zero Python implementation at all. Three targeted fixes for the Python LLM-EVL-001 gap (base implementation, subscript-assignment support, widened shared invocation pattern) were implemented, unit-tested, and verified correct in isolation, then measured against the full 24-repository golden cohort twice: recall did not move. Each remaining miss has its own distinct confound beyond what was fixed (cross-file/class-attribute tracing, cross-module TypeScript tracing, or an intentional raw-results-retained negative boundary).
